description:
Source: bennett-vm/.tmp/sol-vm-queue/cross-repo-beads.md, "ISA 0.9 K81 terminal diagonal inverse versus §6 recompute".

Determination: §6.1 leaves perm provenance unchanged under a diagonal use and §6.4 permits perm-value recompute, while K81 coalesces the maximal terminal matched inverse chain before selecting one cleanup. Counterexample: qalloc d; cx x d; z d; z d; cx x d; qfree d. The written region is identity for both x basis values (and superpositions). Coalescing C=(cx x d; z d), C-adjoint and release, then applying the literal fresh C / XOR / C-adjoint recipe leaves Z on x: for x=1 the original prefix phase survives, whereas written reverse cancels it. The current VM declines recompute for a computing sequence containing Z; that avoids a wrong unitary but is not a ruling on the promised scope, and a blanket ban on these source regions would narrow the contract.

Required normative decision: does the terminal partition exclude diagonal-phase inverse occurrences from the value cleanup, preserving them at their source positions, or does recompute additionally replay/cancel the original phase inverses outside its fresh value computation? Specify exact owner, carrier, caller/callee addresses and phase treatment, including empty/zero-width cases. K81 says every explicit inverse has exactly one owner and no source restriction is added; §6.1 says the value remains perm. Mixed-fat compatibility: this is a local device-module cleanup rule; native host binary/launch boundaries are unaffected (bennett-4ht, fat-object far star: no lock-out). title: §9.4/§11 borrowed owner selection and designated idle sets (borrow_from, gate.ancilla_borrow_from) (from bennett-sched-qm2)
description:
Source: bennett-sched/.tmp/cross-repo-beads.md, "borrowed owner selection and designated idle sets" (local review bead bennett-sched-qm2).

Determination: §9.4 says the caller designates an idle set and §8.2 replaces its owner's charge, but the source call forms and the §11 alloc schema have no owner-selection field and no deterministic default designation, so a checker cannot infer a producer's chosen owner from an opaque frame id. Evidence (C ABI probe): outer mut(t,y), in(x) calls bd(t,x) whose four-CX translation frame borrows b; at capacity 3 it returns INFEASIBLE, at capacity 8/dirty_rate 0.5 it reports time 4, peak 4, occupancy 14; reusing idle caller y would give peak 3 and occupancy 10. Current expansion allocates a separate dirty requirement and records no owner alias. Topology vertices alone do not solve the no-topology case.

Proposed exact schema: extend source alloc decisions with optional borrow_from:[<wire reference>, ...], permitted only for qborrow/dirty acquisitions. A wire reference is exactly one of {invocation:<fully resolved §12.1 context key>,slot:<§9.4 slot id>,bit:<nonnegative integer>} or {allocation:<fully resolved alloc-operation selector>,bit:<nonnegative integer>}. Allocation selectors use the existing fully concrete path/step/phase/generated fields and imply kind=alloc. The array has exactly the acquisition width, in bit order; all referenced bits are distinct, live, held by the direct caller as mutable interface/region bits or live allocation/lease bits, and have the declared/resolved class. Passed callee interface bits, inherited controls, caller read-only slots, overlapping outgoing loans and any owner access overlapping the loan lifetime are forbidden. An incoming lease may be re-lent while held, but its owner must retain the complete lease chain. Unknown references, expired lifetimes, class mismatches or overlapping use reject.

Normative behaviour: supplied borrow_from is the caller's designation. Bind borrowed logical bits to those physical owner bits without acquiring extra physical capacity; retain owner vertices and require alloc.vertices to agree when both occur. Keep every reference-library acquire/release and gate leaf/ordinal unchanged. Require the existing universal T3 condition, including correlated owner states. Split the owner's charging interval around each outgoing loan, replace it by borrower dirty_rate during the loan, count the physical bit once in peaks. A return restores the owner's lease and state. Record aliases by the schedule hash-bound decision, not a producer proof label. For absent borrow_from, specify the existing separate external dirty requirement as the default (no implicit subtraction of an unrelated interface charge), or ratify one deterministic caller idle-set default; current text does not choose. Add class, partial-bundle, nested-lease, read-only/control exclusion, zero-time boundary and topology witnesses, including the exact no-topology t/y/x example.

Analogous gate.ancilla_borrow_from list needed for a selected scheme with dirty ancillae (length equals resolved ancilla count; illegal for native/clean schemes), same exclusions and charging. No unratified field is emitted. This is a contract/mechanics follow-up, not removal of dirty borrowing from scope.

title: ISA 0.9 §11 lacks addresses for hoisted action qregion support
description:
ISA 0.9 requires function-entry qregion support in actions, but §11 gives that support no legal terminal address when the declaration is lexically inside a zero-trip qloop. This prevents a complete source-bound ref@0.9 event stream without inventing ISA rules or rejecting a valid source program.

Normative evidence (published spec/Bennett-ISA-Spec-0.9.md):
- §4.6 qregion (line 1013): "created at function entry (unconditional allocation, X gates from the data image, default zero)" and "scope is the function". The structured grammar permits qregion in a qloop body; no placement restriction excludes it.
- §11 Matching (lines 2474-2487): "Every generated operation has an invocation chain" ending in its own point. The iteration vector contains dynamic repetition counts of enclosing source qloops and "its length is the point's loop nesting depth".
- K64 (lines 2639-2671) defines $construct/$step/$commit/$release "in their containing oracle", requires their own iteration and instance vectors [], and accepts the reserved spellings "for oracle support". It supplies no action-root support addresses.
- K65 (lines 2696-2699) excludes implicit qregion image restoration from explicit-pair carriers, so a cleanup carrier cannot supply the missing address.

Minimal admitted/reversible source (0.9 action signature has bounds:[0], mut:[1]):
action @gap (t:wire mut) () () () ()
regs {  } bounds {0}
^entry():
qloop 0 {
qregion local 0 1
}
x t

The declaration's canonical point is entry:1. Its allocation/release occur once at function entry/exit, although there is no dynamic iteration of its enclosing qloop. [] has the wrong lexical depth; every [i] is out of range. The action has no containing oracle for K64. Omitting the leaves or suppressing allocation would contradict §4.6; rejecting this source would narrow the ISA.

Reproduction: reference-interpreter/tests/source_addressing.rs; headless job environment, cargo test --offline -j4 --manifest-path reference-interpreter/Cargo.toml --test source_addressing -- --test-threads=4 --nocapture. .tmp/sol-ref09/qregion-address-gap.log records successful forward/adjoint execution for t=0,1 and current schedule-validation diagnostics: entry:1/[] -> iteration depth mismatch; entry:1/[0] -> selector out of bounds; $construct/[] and $release/[] -> point must be block:ordinal. These parser errors support, but do not replace, the normative argument above. Source closure hash 439ba7ad235b7ad1663322bc1b7cdf4cffb15d9e798dff7e85d402a9921a20fc.

Exact proposed normative text for spec-owner decision (do not apply in this implementation job):
"For an action or perm_action invocation, function-entry qregion allocations and image-initialisation leaves have terminal pseudo-point $construct, and function-exit image-restoration and release leaves have terminal pseudo-point $release. These leaves are emitted once per invocation, including declarations lexically inside zero-trip qloops or either qif arm. Traverse declarations in canonical source order for construction and reverse declaration order for release. Number leaves contiguously from zero within each pseudo-point, including all cells and image gates, excluding the action body and semantic callees. Their own iteration and instance vectors are []; outer invocation edges retain their actual coordinates. At the action's level they have no step or phase and match only wildcard step/phase. Raw inverse traversal retains forward pseudo-points, generated ordinals, invocation edges and allocation identities while adjointing operations. Path validation admits $construct and $release for action and perm_action support; $step and $commit remain oracle-only. K64's oracle partition is unchanged."

Alternative consistent address rules are a contract decision. Do not resolve by forbidding nested declarations or by changing 0.8. Slice b-isa-spec-fuk.3 remains incomplete and no council round is requested here.

title: K65: define canonical cleanup-pair partition for overlapping call and lifetime inverses
description:
ISA 0.9 K65 §11 says: "Each explicit computing-sequence/cleanup pair has one non-emitting cleanup carrier at its source cleanup point, identified before realisation expansion, even when the cleanup emits no leaves." It continues: "The point is the explicit `quncopy`, `qunload`, `lift.oracle_uncall` or adjoint-call point when that instruction is the cleanup; for an explicitly written inverse sequence ending in `qfree` or `qreturn`, it is that terminating release point (also for an empty inverse sequence)." §6.2 says: "Each cleanup is bound to its exact computing sequence". K80 fixes emitted-leaf ownership once the pair is known, but does not seem to define a unique partition when several computing-sequence/cleanup bindings are possible from the unannotated source.

Reduced source (all separate rows; x is wire[2] in, d is clean owned, mix is a permutation action on the two one-bit mut targets):
entry:0 d = qcopy x
entry:1 action_call @mix (d[0], d[1]) () () ()
entry:2 adj action_call @mix (d[0], d[1]) () () ()
entry:3 quncopy x d
mix: cx a b

Reading A: d's whole computing sequence is rows 0-1 and its written inverse is rows 2-3. One carrier at entry:3 selects the entire inverse, including the adjoint call; row 2 is part of that cleanup and has no independent carrier.
Reading B: rows 1-2 form an explicit matched action/adjoint pair, hence a carrier at entry:2; rows 0-3 form the qcopy/quncopy pair with a carrier at entry:3. Both are explicit pairs and both can independently select realisations. The call pair's pre-call targets are nonzero, so its recompute must preserve the exact source-derived pre-call input history.

These readings differ observably even for reverse (carrier/tie domains), and recompute changes call_index/path/generated domains under K80. A cleanup selector at entry:2 can be ungenerated under A but must select or witness a tie under B. The same ambiguity can arise with a primitive target-local inverse followed by release, and affects complete bound-library call-index validation of fresh cleanup calls.

Please specify deterministic source pair formation/precedence (e.g. maximal whole lifetime sequence versus every explicit call pair, with exact overlap rules), or a published explicit binding representation if the producer must supply one. Add a normative witness for the source above giving every carrier and which source rows it owns. Do not narrow the allowed source programs or delegate observable pair partitioning to a private consumer heuristic.

title: §12.1 adjoint_table lacks a binding to the forward proof/body (from bennett-conformance checker)
description:
Source: bennett-conformance/checker/.tmp/CROSS_REPO_BEADS.md item 5 (sol-checker job; labels requested defect, isa).

Determination: §12.1 adjoint_table lacks a binding to the forward proof/body. §16.3 example 3 says the reverse borrow sequence `cx b t; cx x b; cx b t; cx x b` is not a translation-lemma frame and is covered by adjoint_table, but the structural payload fixes its witness to {} and supplies only integer subclaim indices. §12.3 stores claims per region; variants are opaque producer strings compared bytewise and do not identify a forward body or an adjoint transformation. The text does not say whether a subclaim may name a different region as subject or how a checker binds a forward proof to the reversed region. Guessing that a variant string means adjoint, or accepting an unrelated prior proof, would be unsound; the checker leaves this correspondence unchecked.

Proposed exact replacement in the §12.1 structural payload row: for adjoint_table: { "forward": { "closure_hash", "claim_index" } }. Add immediately after the table: "An adjoint_table witness names a linked forward region and a zero-based claim in that region's certificate record. The checker MUST independently check that claim, then check that the current region's body is the complete §5.3 source adjoint of the named forward body, modulo capture-free renaming of local bindings and positional renaming of interface/classical parameters. Signature widths, region roles, argument types and bounds MUST agree. Primitive adjoints, structured order, unconditional allocations/releases and borrow lifetimes MUST all match; matching only the interface or a chosen basis tuple is insufficient. The forward claim must establish the required preservation/cleanliness relation over the full applicable quantum domain at the same invocation scope; a slice or sampled result cannot discharge a proof obligation. The derived claim inherits that established relation and its proof/evidence scope. Cyclic or unchecked dependencies discharge no obligation. A claim in a region record otherwise names that region as its subject, except the explicitly specified inverse_pair relation. Cross-region structural proof references use the witness above rather than implicit integer indexing."

The spec owner should confirm or replace this binding design; no producer payload extension is accepted before that decision. Related: b-isa-spec-7s0 (borrow-frame claim binding).

title: Token identity aliasing not encoded by K13 tuples (EST-CONTEXT-03; token_aliases) (from bennett-estimate)
description:
Source: bennett-estimate/.tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md, "EST-CONTEXT-03: token identity aliasing". Local owner bennett-estimate.

Determination: K12/K13 fix decimal handling and tuple-only parameter encoding, but §5.3 matched pairs retain token identities as well as tuples, §5.4 produces a fresh token for each successful budget.mint, and §4.1 uncall compares recorded boundary argument values. Equal four-string tuples do not say whether two input operands are one handle or two.

Evidence: bennett-estimate tests/fixtures/token-alias-source-gap.bisa (VM-admitted, object hash cda0f55ff3f299b165453ff9162b051ddf96856a799d22e09499c226bf35c011). Its CC root calls a no-op R function with token a, then uncalls with token b. Same handle at both positions completes in four source steps; two distinct handles for the same tuple fault at the third step. Both encode as args [["1","0","0","0"],["1","0","0","0"]] with the same K13 params_hash. (Counts are derived from the printed instructions, not a VM differential: run-cc reports budget.mint unimplemented.) Q-region consequence: two oracle-call occurrences using a and b may or may not be a K81 matched pair, so cleanup-carrier applicability can depend on the same missing alias relation. Current estimator code raises EST-CONTEXT-03 only when an unresolved equality matters; a conditional step bound remains available.

Proposed normative text (UNADOPTED, preserving identity-based matching): "Token identity context. A resolved invocation additionally carries token_aliases, an array of nonnegative integer identity-class labels. Position zero denotes the separately supplied invocation token; subsequent positions denote token-typed arguments in signature order. Equal labels denote the same valid token identity and require equal tuples; unequal labels denote distinct identities even when their tuples agree. Labels are canonical by first occurrence, starting at zero. This records equality, never a process-local handle. With no token arguments the array is [0]; otherwise the request MUST supply it and a missing or conflicting context is E_ARG. bindings.invocation and schedule bindings carry this token_aliases array; it is copied and compared as part of request/schedule/certificate matching. params_hash remains SHA-256 of the args array. Source forwarding and fixed-binding formation preserve these classes; a successful budget.mint introduces a fresh class attached to its defining occurrence. Nested contexts preserve resolved classes through call paths instead of reconstructing identities from tuple equality. The estimate request accepts token_aliases_jcs and token_aliases_len following params_len; the scheduler exposes bennett_sched_request_set_token_aliases with the same JCS array. Certificate invocation schemas admit token_aliases and require it for scheduled identity-dependent subjects." A different ratified identity/equality rule could resolve it instead. Related: b-isa-spec-8wn (token-to-region binding).

title: §12.3 resource report aggregation for repeated region contexts (resource_contexts) (from bennett-conformance checker)
description:
Source: bennett-conformance/checker/.tmp/CROSS_REPO_BEADS.md item 4.

Determination: §12 does not define resource-report aggregation for repeated region contexts. Witness: root a(t,c) runs `action_call @flip (t) () () ()` then `ctl c action_call @flip (t) () () ()`; flip is `x t`. An exact native X entry matching total controls 0..1 and duration 1 gives the same flip closure two contexts: (forward,0) has one live wire, time 1, qubit_second 1, peak_qubits 1; (forward,1) has two live wires, time 1, qubit_second 2, peak_qubits 2. The region.resources and region.gates_used maps are flat, unlike error/cleanup, and §12 does not say which context they describe, whether they are bounds, or whether they aggregate calls. Max/sum/arbitrary-context would give incompatible answers; classical arguments can make this vary even at the same variant/control key. Repeated-context flat reports remain unchecked.

Proposed exact addition to the region schema: `resource_contexts?: [ { context_key, resources, gates_used, estimate? } ]`. Add after the §12.3 schema: "When a region has exactly one invocation context, its resources/gates_used maps report that invocation. When it has more than one invocation context, resource_contexts MUST contain exactly one record for each §12.1 context, in the same enumeration order, with exact §8.2 accounting and §10.1 encodings where estimate is present. The unkeyed resources/gates_used maps remain required for compatibility but discharge no per-context resource obligation in that case. Checkers MUST reject missing, duplicate or mismatched context records, rather than interpreting unkeyed maps as sums or maxima."

title: Rung 4: decide the label of an exhaustive claim over a region fixed to classical bytes (North Star §5.1 vs §12.2 K74)
description:

Dialect 0.2.10 §25.2 lists this as open: "The ISA should say whether an exhaustive claim over the remaining components, with the fixed region prepared from classical bytes (`qprep`, `bennett_qreg_prepare`), is a proof for that region content." The gate does not block on this: it requires today's label, `evidence` with the exact fraction, and never reports proof (DESIGN.md §4). title: Target §8: QEC, hierarchy and code-distance bindings for imported resource models (targets gyp)
description:
Source: b-targets-gyp; North Star §7 row "Qualtran, Azure RE" promises imported models. ISA 0.9 §8.3 imports decides only {quantity:[resource,factor]}, so numeric quantities import as named resources (done in bennett-targets, including physical failure probabilities as count resources, never as epsilon). §8 does not decide: an Azure qecScheme logicalCycleTime or physicalQubitsPerLogicalQubit formula is a function of codeDistance and of hardware quantities; §8.1 v admits no codeDistance and no imported quantity; a distillation factory is a hierarchy of logical operations; Qualtran AlgorithmSummary counts are symbolic. Maintainer/council decision needed; nothing in bennett-targets presumes the outcome and these inputs stay loud errors.

PROPOSED SPEC TEXT, new §8.5 (target 0.10):

"### 8.5 Imported model parameters
"parameters"?: { "<name>": { "value": n | null, "from"?: "<model>.<quantity>" } } is optional and unknown fields reject. A parameter with value null MUST be bound by the consumer before evaluation; an unbound parameter is a load-time error. `imports.<model>` gains an optional "formulas": { "<quantity>": expr }, evaluated exactly like §8.1 with these extra bound variables: {"param":"<name>"}. A formula is evaluated only to produce a quantity, which then converts through `map` as [resource, factor]; it never contributes to a gates entry's epsilon. Formula evaluation binds no eps, so `log2inv_eps` and `eps_decade` are load-time errors in it. Physical failure probabilities are count resources summed per §8.2. They bound nothing about operator-norm error and MUST NOT be read as `epsilon` (§8.1). A hierarchy (code block, factory) is expressed as an imported model with its own quantities; §8 assigns no composition rule, and a composed logical estimate is a certificate attached to the object, not a target field."

Exact questions for the decision: (a) whether code-distance selection belongs in the target or the certificate; (b) whether a formula language beyond §8.1 expr (power, sqrt, as in Azure formula strings) is admitted, since §8.1 has no exponentiation and crossingPrefactor*(p/pth)^((d+1)/2) cannot be written in it. Proposed: add "pow" (2) with an integer exponent only, exact rationals, in formula context only.

title: Launch ABI lacks VM stepping, snapshots, prefix reversal and last-error interfaces
description: ISA 0.8 §10 lists run/wait/suspend/resume/reverse/close but no stepping, snapshot or diagnostic accessor. Its reverse condition is "Reverse eligibility: COMPLETED; no measure" and §7.4 describes history reversal, not a host reverse-to-history-length entry point. VM docs/PROGRESS.md needs six explicitly private functions: bennett_run_step, bennett_run_snapshot, bennett_snapshot_jcs, bennett_snapshot_free, bennett_run_reverse_to, bennett_last_error, plus opaque bennett_snapshot_t. Snapshots provide immutable owned diagnostic JCS; reverse_to allows SUSPENDED/COMPLETED/FAILED prefixes and suspends afterwards; last_error is thread-local until the next failing call. Record and decide these host capabilities in ISA 0.9, including names, signatures, states and lifetimes. None is invented in the ISA 0.8 headers.

title: Scheduling ABI leaves request buffer lifetimes and response ownership underspecified
description: ISA 0.8 §11 declares "bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_object(bennett_sched_request_t*, const uint8_t*, size_t);" and setters for target, params and strings, but never says when their inputs are copied or how long they must remain live. §10 explicitly says "Arguments and the entropy tape are copied at bennett_run; the caller may free its buffers afterwards." No corresponding scheduling statement exists. §11 lists request/response frees and pointer accessors but does not explicitly extend §10 object/pointer lifetime rules to them, specify response independence from the request, required setters/defaults, or status-versus-outcome failures. Define these scheduling call contracts in ISA 0.9. The published header declares only the specified functions and makes no copying/lifetime promises beyond the text.

title: Launch ABI lacks general invalid-argument and allocation-failure contracts
description: ISA 0.8 §10 defines "BENNETT_E_ARG, BENNETT_E_NOMEM" but not general NULL/index validity, output preservation on failure or allocation-failure coverage. It declares status-less accessors such as "uint64_t bennett_result_fault(const bennett_result_t*, size_t i);" and "const uint8_t* bennett_request_payload(const bennett_request_t*, size_t* len);". VM docs/PROGRESS.md requires valid objects/out-length pointers, fails loudly on misuse, maps recoverable argument-vector allocation failure to E_NOMEM, permits allocator aborts elsewhere, and accepts NULL in matching frees. These are VM interpretations, not stated public preconditions. Specify a general failure/precondition contract in ISA 0.9 rather than inventing one in the headers.

title: Launch ABI does not specify host thread synchronization or progress guarantees
description: ISA 0.8 §10 says "bennett_wait blocks until the run leaves RUNNING" and "A run owns the registers and memory it touches exclusively while not CLOSED." These rules do not define thread safety of calls on the same program or whether suspend/reply may run concurrently with wait, nor whether progress is autonomous or cooperative. VM docs/PROGRESS.md chooses cooperative execution and externally synchronized per-program calls. Specify synchronization and progress in ISA 0.9 so host programs can implement wait/suspend safely across providers; do not narrow promised execution capabilities.

title: Effect tape iterator has no specified end-of-tape result

Its status enum has no EOF enumerator, and exhaustion, output preservation and repeat calls at EOF have no stated contract. VM docs/PROGRESS.md chooses E_INVALID_STATE, an explicit diagnostic, and untouched outputs. Specify EOF semantics in ISA 0.9 without conflating an implementation convention with normative ABI.

title: ISA: lprocs cannot pass tokens or classical args to lifted calls
description: 0.8 §4.2 says tk of lift.oracle_call is a classical argument of the calling oracle, and §3.7 lets an lproc read only its params and locations; draft 0.9 E17.14 makes explicit that lifted-call args are classical arguments of the calling oracle, never locations (a location as a classical arg would be superposed). Consequence: a nested oracle call or a parametrised perm_call made from inside an lproc has no way to obtain a token or classical args. Construction today: inline the call into the oracle body or pass values as in-wires/params instead of args; tokens have no such path. Possible fix: a per-oracle classical-argument environment readable by lprocs (pseudo-locations visible in the closure), or token params for lprocs. title: G-12: Oracle entry state from the caller's run-time classical memory, at native addresses
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2b (G-12).

Verdict: New candidate gap (not in the dialect's list).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.7 'Initial allocator state ... storage of mem all zero except global images'; §7.2 'for each interface region ... a base address; all ranges disjoint'; §7.1 one layout for CC and lifted memory, so an interface region can never overlap a CC global or CC heap address.

Blocks: Rung 7 at kernel scale: correct in 0.8 through the replay-plus-copy prologue of dialect O-07, but every oracle invocation pays O(snapshot) steps, each a full memory dispatch, which dominates 7(c). Rung 4 is not affected with the VFS-image design (phase 2 should confirm).

title: I5: Done-invariance of idle steps (variable-time readiness; candidate T7)
description:

State as a property (candidate T7): on a branch that reached HALT at step t, every later forward step is the identity on (ins, tgt, fr, result_val, locations, cells) and leaves its frame at |0>. Make the step variant that controls the successor XOR and both commit exchanges on `not at_HALT` the reference (section 3.6 steps 3-4), add a suite-B test that an idle step is the identity, and add the `pc = HALT` predicate as the 'done' projector in the formal model (section 14). title: I1: Pebbled / checkpointed oracle realisations
description:
Source: worklog/001_2026-10-28_bootstrap.md ('Open items (pre-bd issue list)')
Id: I1

The section 5.2 construction keeps B frames. Bennett-1989 pebbling (and the Knill-1995 strategies in Bennett.jl src/pebble/) trade frames for O(log B) checkpoints at polylog time. T6 arguably admits it as a section 5.7 transformation, but section 11 has no schedule kind to bind or cost a checkpoint and T2 is stated only for the full-history realisation. Spec change: name checkpointed realisations in section 5.7, add a schedule binding and a section 17 default (full history). Core, S1 with default.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — binary pebbling recurrence T(k)=3T(k-1) gives 3^ceil(log2 B) evaluations and O(S log B) checkpoint bits. Polylog-time claim is not established. Exact proposed expansion/resource binding and tests are in the evidence note; 4(c)/7(c) space only. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: I2: Structure recovery of bounded data-dependent loops
description:
Source: worklog/001_2026-10-28_bootstrap.md ('Open items (pre-bd issue list)')
Id: I2

`qloop n while cond` needs `cond` computed before the loop from wires the body does not modify, so a Collatz-style exit cannot use it; the dispatch-free form is `qloop B_iter` with the body predicated on a 'still running' flag. Give that idiom (or a `qloop n until flag` form) in section 4.6 / 5.7 so the specialiser does not pay per-step dispatch over the whole program. Core, S1. (Plan risk R5 notes rung-4 option (c) estimates need this.)
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — structure recovery already permitted by T6; active selectors cannot be modified. Immutable-input prefix selectors or retained history give constructions. Preserving the original row-budget fault boundary is mandatory. Rung 4(c) usefulness depends on implementation proofs. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: Say that classical memory and the allocation table persist across runs of a loaded program
description: Dialect draft 0.3 §6.5 keeps ids of live registers in device memory across device-entry calls, and 0.2's handle-cross-entry examples assume the same. A later run of the program starts from the memory, allocation table and bump pointer the previous CLOSED run left, or the entry state if that run was REVERSED.' title: Width-parametric region signature for oracles whose interface width is a run-time value (dialect 0.3 G-17)
description: Dialect draft 0.3 §8.4 realises an oracle whose interface width or descriptor extent is a run-time value by static dispatch over every valid width (maintainer D15), because ISA 0.9 §5.1/§9.1 region signatures have literal wire widths and a qreg[*] transfer (§3.3) is only width-checked against a fixed slot. The capability exists on 0.9, so this is not a blocker, but the construction names up to 2^64 reference objects, so no plugin can emit it in full (dialect §24 D34). Requested ISA text for a later version, evidence only (§0.3 style): 'K-new. A region signature MAY declare a width parameter: oracle @o [n] (x:wire[n] in) (t:wire[n]) (f:wire[F]) () (). An oracle_call binds n from qreg.width of its first parametric operand, checked equal across operands as §3.3 binding checks; the interface hash covers the parametric signature, and the closure is expanded per n with the budget and schedule keyed on (n, tuple).' Alternative: load-time object instantiation for a named width set. Dialect 0.3 does not depend on it.

title: ISA: measuring registers wider than 128 bits (efficiency item)

Construction on 0.9: copy 128-bit slices into fresh qreg[128] targets with a permutation action (cx per wire, as EN ISA-6 measure_same), measure the copies, reset the collapsed source wire by wire via run-time slices and classical dispatch, then free. Capability kept; a direct qreg.split or wide measure is an efficiency candidate. Raised by the 0.9 draft job (b-isa-spec-so1), open question in spec/isa-0.9.PROGRESS.md.

title: ISA-11: Host memory by reference at native addresses (launch argument)
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-11).

Verdict: Real gap for pointer-rich host data. Copy-in/copy-out of flat bytes works through hostcall. Pointers inside host structures cannot keep their values on the device, because CC memory cannot place an object at a host address.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §10: INT(width, bytes) to iN ..., F64 to f64, QREG to qreg[n] ..., TOKEN to token. 'Arguments and the entropy tape are copied'; hostcall copies [ptr, ptr+len) into a request and writes the reply. §7.1: CC memory consists of globals and a bump heap; there is no allocation at a chosen address.

Blocks: Blocks no rung (rungs run whole programs on the device). Blocks NS §3.3/§5 partial compilation over shared pointer-rich data. Dialect: D25, O-08.

Change: a launch argument kind `MEM(addr, len)`, or a CC `alloc.at addr n` within a host-window range of the layout.

title: ISA-8: R-tier fault propagation to the calling CC code; faulted run not reversible
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-8).

Verdict: Real gap. The ISA does not say what the CC caller of a faulted R call observes, and a FAILED run cannot be reversed even though §7.4 calls the faulted state 'reversed like any prefix'.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.1 'R fault record'; §7.4 'fault record | cause code (§5.4) and location; terminal faulted state, reversed like any prefix'. §10 'Reverse eligibility: COMPLETED'.

Blocks: Blocks no rung (rungs 3/6 require fault-free runs).

Change: an R call returns a fault status to its CC caller, and runs ending in an R fault are reverse-eligible.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — exact proposal makes uncaught R faults terminal to the CC run and permits reversal of fully logged FAILED prefixes with no measurement/unverified release. No extra R result/status convention required. Fault-free rungs 3/6 unaffected. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-9: Borrowed wires outside static Q regions (borrowing driven from CC)
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-9).

Change: allow qborrow/qreturn in CC with a borrow-frame discipline.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — a correct dirty-borrow user works with clean wires, or can use an existing verified Q borrow frame. Charge actual clean occupancy; do not claim dirty-rate savings for that fallback. No rung dependency. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-7: Fault code of a CC trap in launch results
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-7).

Verdict: Real gap (wording). No rule maps a CC trap cause to a §5.4 code. The only mapping given is §17 item 14 (unclean qreg.free -> FAULT_UB_TRAP).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.1 says only 'CC trap' (udiv, load, trap, ...); §10 'Fault records are read by bennett_result_nfaults / bennett_result_fault (codes of §5.4 ...)'.

Blocks: Blocks no rung. Also needed for the dialect's reversible-budget fault code (dialect issue 1.4-e).

Change: a table in ISA §4.1 from trap cause to §5.4 code (div0 -> 5, MIN/-1 -> 6, out-of-allocation -> 7, trap -> 4, alloc failure -> 2), and a CC/R `fault C` instruction so dialect-level traps (budget, T-*) report their own code.
notes:
[isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — specify CC/R trap cause mapping and explicit fault C, with frame/reversal and launch result rules. R step counters already exist; exact exhaustion code1 uses this instruction. Code10 may describe virtualised coherent entropy. See also zero-cause defect b-isa-spec-7qu. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.
Rung 3 measured consumer dependency (2026-11-01), estimate medium (480 minutes). Dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §11.5 determining sentence: "On ISA 0.8 a module has verdict blocked:BD-B-ISA7 if its device program contains an R-tier variant reached as an R entry: a reversible region candidate invoked outside generation, or the §19.2 whole-program R entry." §17.6: "Before each counted materialised LLVM instruction, check that one step remains, then consume it before execution; otherwise raise code 1 before executing the instruction." Required instruction: R fault C, including mandatory pre-instruction fault 1, preserves prefix history and exact code. Exact contract inspection: git -C /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-dialect-spec show 023f5a771a814270634db3be9cfde88ded69f975:spec/Bennett-Dialect-Spec.md . Gate prerequisite reports BD-B-ISA7; actual musl production is earlier blocked by missing sysroot, and the isolated R-mode opt probe rejects options. Fixed means resolve/adopt the published ISA 0.9 typed-fault contract (now published alongside 0.8), implement executor/producer support and explicitly update consumer contract pins after verification; never mutate ISA 0.8 or pass generic trap off as typed fault. No narrowing of the North Star acceptance. Evidence /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-3/20261101T125019.671846Z.
close_reason: Not a remaining defect in published ISA 0.9: accepted §0.2 K5 explicitly names bd 221; §4.1 fault and §4.9 give the implicit cause table, exact nonzero C through 2^64-1 (zero ->4), one terminal record/no successor/no later caller effect and intact prefix; §7.4/§10/T4 specify FAILED-run restoration. The consumer correctly blocks every ISA-0.8 R entry per dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §11.5/§17.6. That real implementation and explicit contract-pin migration prerequisite is retained as open b-isa-spec-fuk; closing this historical wording issue does NOT clear BD-B-ISA7 or rung 3. README and pass-XI progress record the migration obligations. No frozen 0.8, normative 0.9, K row, catalog or sibling-pin change.

title: ISA-5: Two simultaneous slices of one qreg
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-5).

Verdict: Real gap (efficiency). Workarounds in 0.8: one `qreg[1]` per wire with static dispatch (O(n^2) for gate2, O(n^3) for gate3, static widths only); or a quantum-addressed gate in an action (index materialised into wires by an oracle with args, then `qpred (a==k)` per k: O(n) gates).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.3: `q2 = qreg.slice q lo len` ... q viewed; q2 MUST be the operand of exactly one region call and of nothing else ... any use of q while viewed is ill-formed. Indexed operand `w[i]` (literal i).

Blocks: Blocks no rung.

Change: `qreg.slices q (lo_1,len_1) ... (lo_k,len_k)` producing disjoint views consumed by one region call.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — one joint-parent action accesses both indexed wires without simultaneous views; runtime indices dispatch to static actions. Proposed slice wording restores VIEWED pre-state on inverse call and LIVE parent on inverse slice. No rung dependency. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-4: qreg of run-time width; qreg values in memory or tables
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-4).

Verdict: Real gap. Blocks run-time-sized registers and handle collections whose size is known only at run time (NS §3.1 handle tables, §4.1/§4.2 dynamic allocation; Bennett.jl's vectors of qubits).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.3: `qreg[n]` is a type with literal n; `q = qreg.new cls n`. §3.2: handles live only in the 'classical environment'; classical memory is 'byte-addressed'. §4.1 has no instruction that stores, loads or converts a qreg. §10 binds `QREG` to `qreg[n]` with the register's n.

Blocks: Blocks no rung if rung 4's register width is a build-time constant. Dialect issues: B-07, B-24.

Change: `qreg[*]` with run-time n, plus either qreg storable in CC memory as an opaque id (`qreg.id` / `qreg.from_id`, the latter trapping on stale ids) or a CC register table `qtab.get/set`.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — dynamic qreg[*], width/id/from_id and shared alias ledger specify uniform dynamic widths and ordinary handle-table lookup. Static register files already work; unbounded instance count alone is not an impossibility proof because recursion retains registers. No fixed-width demo rung blocker. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-3: qinplace has no ins / mem / args operands
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-3).

Verdict: Real gap for `qinplace`. Writing the macro out by hand in an action does not substitute, because §6.2 binds every cleanup to 'its exact computing sequence' (reverse or recompute, §6.4) and the `ginv` call that cleans `t` is neither. Oracle args are NOT a gap (ISA §4.7, §5.1, §9.1); the JCS spelling of types in `"args"` is an editorial item (use the §16.2 type spelling as JCS strings).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.5: `qinplace @g @ginv tk x` ... Sem: `t = qalloc any n; f = qalloc any F; oracle_call @g tk (x) t f; qexch x t; oracle_call @ginv tk (x) t f; qfree t; qfree f` has no ins, mem or args. By contrast §4.7 `oracle_call @o tk (ins..) tgt fr (mem..) (args..)`, §5.1 `(args n: i64)`, §9.1 `"args":[types]`.

Blocks: Blocks no rung; blocks NS §3.1/§4.2 parametrised in-place updates (`x += a` with run-time a, controlled modular multiplication by a run-time constant). Dialect issue: 1.4-f.

Change: `qinplace @g @ginv tk x (ins..) (mem..) (args..)`, the §4.5 macro passing them to both oracle_calls; §6.1 transfer `x: perm with S_x U ins U cells U Pi`.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — extend certified qinplace to ins/mem/args, state inverse-pair cleanup exception and parameter/version provenance. Explicit compute/swap/inverse-call is not automatically an exact-sequence cleanup. Finite synthesis/library bijections exist; no demo rung requires the general declared-pair contract. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-1: CC instruction to build a budget token from run-time values
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-1).

Verdict: Real gap, partly. A host-supplied run-time budget is not a gap: the driver's launch stub mints the token from the host value and passes it as TOKEN. A budget computed on the device (e.g. from measurement results, NS §4.2) is a real gap.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.1 lists no token-producing instruction. Tokens come only from the launch API: `bennett_status bennett_budget(bennett_program_t*, const char* region, uint64_t steps, uint64_t heap, uint64_t stack, uint64_t depth, bennett_token* out);` and bind as `TOKEN` to `token` (§10).

Blocks: Blocks no rung (host-supplied run-time budgets are already possible).

Change: CC `tk = budget.mint @region s h st d` with the §5.4 validation as a CC trap.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap in uniform device minting — host tokens and finite dispatch already work, even after measurement. Exact proposed CC budget.mint binds the immutable tuple, schedule and reversal ledger; T2 holds for each fixed classical outcome. No rung depends on minting. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.
